title: Add kernel selection v2 canary scenarios (v1 vs v2) across GPU SKUs + seq buckets
author: Marcus Reed
release_notes:
- perf-canary: add kernel selection v2 comparison scenarios (v1 vs v2) across A100/H100/L40S with short/medium/long seq buckets
- perf-canary: add alert thresholds tuned for selection regressions (p95/p99 + error + throughput) with SKU-aware grouping
- perf-canary: add dashboards links + runbook pointers in scenario docs
body:
## Summary
Adds a new perf-canary scenario pack to compare kernel selection v1 vs v2 under realistic prompt/decode regimes across heterogeneous fleets (A100/H100/L40S). This is intended to be the primary signal for runtime 1.21 staged rollout gating.

## Why
Kernel auto-selection v2 changes decision logic keyed on (model family, seq-length regime, GPU SKU). We need canary coverage that (a) is SKU-aware, (b) buckets workloads in a way that catches long-context tail-latency spikes, and (c) emits stable, actionable alerts when v2 mis-selects.

## What changed
- New scenario group `kernel_selection/v2_compare` that runs each workload twice per target: once with selector v1, once with selector v2 enabled via runtime flags.
- Coverage matrix:
  - Model families: llama (Llama-3.x), mistral (Mistral), qwen (Qwen2.5)
  - GPUs: A100-80GB, H100-SXM, L40S
  - Seq buckets (prefill/decode regimes):
    - short: prefill~512-1k / decode~128-256
    - medium: prefill~4k / decode~256-512
    - long: prefill~16k-32k / decode~128-256 (tail-risk bucket)
  - Mixed workload scenario that alternates short/long to stress regime classification stability.
- Added comparison report that tags results with `selector_version=v1|v2`, `gpu_sku_normalized`, `model_family`, `seq_bucket`, and `workload_id`.
- Added alerting thresholds (defaults) and grouping policy:
  - p95 latency regression: warn at +5%, page at +10% (v2 relative to v1) per (model_family, gpu_sku_normalized, seq_bucket)
  - p99 latency regression: warn at +8%, page at +15% (same grouping)
  - throughput regression (tok/s): warn at -3%, page at -7%
  - error rate (5xx/runtime errors): page if absolute >0.2% or delta >0.1% (whichever is greater)
  - stability guard: suppresses paging if N<30 runs for a bucket (still emits a warn + marks bucket as low-sample)

## Notes on SKU normalization
We normalize provider instance strings into `gpu_sku_normalized` (e.g., `a100-80gb`, `h100-sxm`, `l40s`) to avoid alert cardinality and to match how runtime v2 registry keys SKUs. This is intentionally coarse; MIG and vendor-specific variants are folded into the parent SKU for canary gating.

## How to run
- Local (dev): `perf-canary run --scenario kernel_selection/v2_compare --target local_gpu`
- CI (nightly): `kernel-selection-v2-compare` job
- Ad hoc (pre-canary): `perf-canary run --scenario kernel_selection/v2_compare --target hosted_canary --set selector_v2=1`

## Related
- Runtime changes: redwood/pr-28460 (feature gate), pr-28452 (SKU-aware registry), pr-28439 (seq bucketing)
- Epic: ENG-4821

## Checklist
- [x] Scenarios cover long-context + mixed workloads
- [x] Metrics include selector_version, gpu_sku_normalized, model_family, seq_bucket
- [x] Alert thresholds reviewed with SRE (Aisha/Allison)
- [x] CI runtime < 40 min per target pool (measured on A100)
- [x] Docs added for oncall interpretation + links to rollout dashboards

## Risk
Low. perf-canary only; no production runtime changes. Primary risk is alert noise from low sample sizes or label explosion; addressed via normalization + N threshold.

conversation: Claire Dubois (review): The long bucket looks good, but can we make sure decode-heavy cases are represented? Some regressions show up when decode dominates. Also, please document the exact distributions (p50/p90 prefill length) in the scenario doc so we can compare across revisions.
Marcus Reed (author): Good call. Added `medium_decode_heavy` variant (prefill~2k/decode~1k) and updated docs with the generated distribution summary table + seed. Pushed in 0b8c4aa.

Allison Grant (review): Please keep label cardinality under control. `gpu_sku` from the agent includes cloud instance naming; we should normalize before it hits alerts. Also suggest grouping alerts by model_family rather than model_id to avoid churn when model revisions roll.

Marcus Reed (author): Implemented `gpu_sku_normalized` and switched alert grouping to (model_family, gpu_sku_normalized, seq_bucket). Still emitting raw `gpu_sku` in debug logs but not in metrics. Added note in docs.

Aisha Bello (review): Thresholds: +5% p95 warn is fine, but for p99 I’d prefer we page at +15% and include an error-rate clause. Also we need a low-sample gate—paging on a single outlier run will be noisy.
Marcus Reed (author): Updated to +8% warn / +15% page on p99 and added error-rate page condition. Added N<30 suppression for paging with a separate warn + annotation so we still see it.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Can we add a small check that compares v2 vs v1 selection distribution and flags when v2 chooses a kernel that’s not in the expected candidate set for that bucket? That’s usually a config drift issue.

Marcus Reed (author): Added a lightweight ‘unexpected_kernel’ counter that only increments when v2 returns a kernel name outside the configured registry for that (sku, model_family) pair. It’s warn-only (no page) and linked in docs for triage.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI runtime: the full matrix will be expensive. Can we ensure nightly runs one GPU per day and rotates, while PR runs a reduced subset?
Marcus Reed (author): Done. PR CI runs A100-only short+long for llama+mistral; nightly rotates (A100/H100/L40S) and runs full matrix. Documented in ci/jobs/nightly.yml.
Claire Dubois (approval): Approved. Please keep the distribution summary stable (seed pinned) so we can compare trends week-over-week.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved with normalization changes.
Aisha Bello (approval): Approved. Thresholds + low-sample suppression look good.
